title: Citizens and the state during crisis: Public authority, private behaviour and the Covid‐19 pandemic in France

selected_claim.evidence_location: Table 1, “Determinants of reported compliance 16–17 March,” pre-speech results; section “Estimating reports of compliance before and after the Macron speech.”
selected_claim.evidence_summary: In the pre-speech subsample, LREM partisanship is positively associated with reporting high compliance (Model 1 logit coefficient 0.623, SE 0.375; marked significant at p < 0.05 using the paper’s one-tailed test). The paper estimates that partisanship shifts the predicted probability of high compliance from 40% to 52% for typical respondents.
selected_claim.x: Attachment to La République En Marche (LREM), the incumbent president’s party, measured as co-partisanship with the government.
selected_claim.y: Self-reported compliance with government directives, coded as high compliance when the behavioral index is 9 or above on a 0–10 scale.
selected_claim.target_population: French adults in the nationally representative ENEF panel who were interviewed before President Macron’s 16 March 2020 televised address.

evidence_summary: The focal paper examines whether co-partisanship with the incumbent government is associated with reported compliance with government directives among French adults interviewed before the president's 16 March 2020 address. The specified pre-speech estimate is logistic regression (Table 1, Model 1) adjusted for presidential approval, health-risk acceptance, perceived public-health and economic threats, extreme-left and extreme-right ideology, personal health, sex, age, education, income, partnership status, and employment. The built evidence queue contains one linked paper and no additional findings; causal evidence beyond the focal study is not available in the queue.

limitations: The evidence queue contains only the focal paper and no additional findings, so independent causal corroboration is unavailable.
The focal outcome is self-reported compliance, and the binary high-compliance threshold derived from the 0–10 index may not represent all dimensions or levels of adherence.
The adjustment specification does not establish that all sources of confounding were addressed; the provided claim does not supply effect estimates or additional author caveats.
